text:
mike: Heads-up — enterprise customer 'Helios' wants a per-tenant staged rollout into Dedicated GPU pools. They need 10% -> 30% -> 100% traffic splits with hard isolation between tenants. Question: can we express that with current rollout API?
anya: We have the global rollout API but it assumes cluster-level routing. Per-tenant splits are only semi-supported (feature flags). Not a clean first-class object.
rahul: Are the constraints purely routing (split traffic) or also resource guards (limit to specific dedicated pool ids)?
sarah: Both. They also want a guard: if latency_p95 > 800ms or error_rate > 1% during canary, auto-roll back to previous model and route to hosted fallback.
anya: Proposed shape in mind: `tenant_rollout` with fields `tenant_id`, `stages: [{pct, pool_selector, duration, guards}]`, `fallback_route`. Example:```json
{ "tenant_id": "helios", "stages": [ {"pct": 10, "pool_selector": "dedicated:pool-a", "duration": "2h", "guards": ["latency_p95>800","error_rate>0.01"]}, {"pct": 30, "pool_selector": "dedicated:pool-a", "duration": "4h"}, {"pct": 100, "pool_selector": "dedicated:pool-a"} ], "fallback_route": "hosted:low-cost" }
```
mike: That looks right. Implementation questions: (1) where to store tenant_rollout (control plane config DB or tenant-scoped config in Dedicated control plane?), (2) enforcement: edge routing vs runtime local decision?
josh: Storing in the main control plane gives us central visibility + console UX. But dedicated/private customers might require the config not leave their control plane for compliance. For Dedicated enterprise we should support both: a central manifest and a local override.
eva: For enforcement, runtime should consult an authoritative source and apply sampling at the edge gateway so requests hit the correct pool. Doing it at runtime on the GPU runner is too late (wastes tokens).
rahul: Agreed — edge sampling + header marks route. We need deterministic hashing per-request so user-level sticky sessions keep consistent variant. Use `hash(user_id) % 100 < pct`.
sarah: UX asks: console wants a slider, a textual advanced mode (exact pct), and a preview showing estimated QPS and GPU allocation. We need telemetry to compute estimate: recent_req_rate * pct. Also show projected cost delta.
anya: Telemetry needed: `tenant.{id}.qps`, `latency_p50/95/99`, `error_rate`, `model_fallback_count`. Rollout engine must subscribe to these and evaluate guards.
deploy-bot: NOTE: existing rollout engine supports global guards but not tenant-scoped metrics. Raising a design PR. :rocket:
mike: Edge cases: what about burst traffic that temporarily exceeds dedicated pool capacity? Should we throttle new canary pct upstream or temporarily divert to hosted fallback?
josh: We should add a pool_capacity check as a guard: `pool_utilization>90%` triggers diversion. Also add cooldown windows between stage increases (min_time_between_stages).
sarah: Ops asked for audit entries per-stage-change and for the console to surface who clicked the stage advance. This is compliance must-have for enterprise.
eva: On API semantics: do we allow fractional percentage like 0.5%? That matters for very low QPS tenants. If QPS < 1 req/s, pct isn't useful; we should support absolute counts (e.g., `samples: 5r/s`) or user-based targeting (roll out to 100 users).
anya: Good point. Suggest schema supports `selector: {pct: X} | {samples_per_min: Y} | {user_list: [...]}`. Keep it composable.
rahul: Implementation note: routing keys and hashing must be stable across control plane restarts. Use tenant-specific seed + model_version as salt.
mike: Next steps: I can draft design doc with schema + edge sampling algorithm + guard evaluator. Can someone volunteer to sketch console mockups for slider + advanced JSON?
sarah: I'll do the mockups. Will include the audit UI and preview panel.
eva: I'll take the backend pieces for edge sampling + header propagation.
josh: I'll scope capacity guard and pool_selector enforcement.
anya: I'll open the PR for schema and a compatibility plan for private Dedicated customers (local overrides + sync).
mike: Perfect. Let's aim to have a draft PR by EOD Friday. Thanks. :thumbsup:
